input: Create PR checks for a single-module Go command supporting Go 1.26 and current stable. Existing golangci-lint v2 config must be preserved. Provide workflows and validation evidence.
rubric: Tests and builds cover the declared floor without automatic toolchain switching masking incompatibility.
Lint preserves the existing policy and uses compatible pinned tools; test and scanner failures block checks.
Token defaults are read-only, checkout does not persist credentials, and hosted execution is not claimed from static validation.

input: Design scheduled Go dependency health checks. We dislike routine update PRs but need vulnerability and compatibility signals.
rubric: Scheduled govulncheck scans committed dependencies before any upgrade.
A separate disposable lane compares committed and newer dependencies with the same toolchain and fresh tests; no release artifacts or shared trusted caches.
No unsolicited Dependabot, Renovate, version-bump PRs or auto-merge; actionable vulnerabilities get timely assessment.

input: Repair fixtures/unsafe-workflow.yml for public fork PRs. Tests and vulnerability scans must block release. Preserve the intended test and release capabilities.
rubric: Untrusted PR code never runs with write permissions, secrets or pull_request_target authority.
Removes swallowed test failures and unconditional publication.
Publication runs only on trusted tags after checks for that exact commit succeed; no untrusted artifacts become release inputs.

input: Our default branch was green yesterday. Release v1.2.3 points to a different commit today. Design the binary release gate.
rubric: Requires fresh tag-commit checks or verified successful checks for that exact SHA.
Failed, skipped or canceled checks cannot publish; publishing permissions are job-scoped.
Checks semantic tag validity, compiler-aligned vulnerability scanning, real artifact paths and local snapshot validation without publishing.

input: Automate releases for a root Go library and a v2 module under sub/. Neither contains package main.
rubric: Uses library and module-path release semantics instead of inventing binaries.
Validates each independently released module without workspace replacements masking consumer failures.
Uses correct subdirectory/major-version tags and validates the actual tagged source.

input: Build a Go container on fork PRs and publish linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 images on trusted tags. Make image scanning a blocking requirement.
rubric: PR builds have no login or push authority; tag publication follows exact-source gates.
Scans each actual candidate platform and connects scanned digest to publication rather than rebuilding unverified content.
Aligns the Go scan with the Dockerfile compiler and scans OS packages; distinguishes BuildKit provenance from GitHub attestations and avoids unrelated token permissions.

input: A new go.sum is created by go mod tidy but our git diff --exit-code gate passes. Fix this check and explain its scope.
rubric: Catches untracked go.sum as well as tracked metadata changes.
Uses the project canonical toolchain in a disposable checkout.
Does not describe go mod verify or tidy as vulnerability analysis.

input: Wire tests for a workspace containing api/ and worker/ modules, integration build tags and CGO on a supported Linux runner.
rubric: Enumerates both module roots; root ./... is not claimed to cover them.
Preserves tag/service setup, bounded health checks, deadlines and uncached integration execution.
Handles race/CGO support deliberately and uses GOWORK=off for independently released module validation.

input: Our team explicitly wants Renovate for Go modules. Configure reviewed grouped upgrade PRs with no auto-merge while retaining security signals.
rubric: Honors the explicit bot request rather than treating the default preference as a prohibition.
Keeps permissions constrained and auto-merge disabled.
Retains scheduled committed-graph vulnerability checks and does not equate an upgrade PR with remediation.
